title: Spain vs. England—Nations League: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack8:00 PM ESTA lot is at stake in the Spanish capital. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images/VisionhausSpain and England lock horns in Madrid on Sunday evening with top spot in UEFA Nations League Group A3 up for grabs.

While the world champion currently boasts the advantage after beating the Three Lions 3–2 at Wembley at the start of the group phase, England’s superior goal difference, largely thanks to its 7–0 beatdown of Croatia, means that victory for the Three Lions in the Spanish capital would see them usurp their hosts and qualify for next March’s quarterfinals as group winners.
Both nations were victorious on Matchday 5, with England bypassing a more spirited Croatia 2–1 and Spain easing past 10-man Czechia 2–0 away from home.

So, it all comes down to this. Thomas Tuchel has labeled the upcoming bout a “final,” with Spain currently the team to beat in international soccer, and not merely because it got its hands on the World Cup trophy in the summer. Luis de la Fuente’s team has lost just once in 43 games (on penalties to Portugal)—a run dating back to March 2024.

It’s an outstanding team, and exactly where Tuchel’s England wants to be. The reverse fixture was a barnstorming encounter, and the pair are projected to put on a similarly exhilarating show at the Metropolitano this weekend.

Spain came from behind to beat England in the reverse fixture. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesEngland is searching for its most significant non-major tournament triumph since defeating Spain 3–2 in October 2018. That victory proved that its World Cup journey in the summer was no fluke, and that Sir Gareth Southgate was building something rather special at St. George’s Park after years of disarray.
The Three Lions ran riot on the counterattack that day, although the match is best remembered for Eric Dier’s scything challenge on Sergio Ramos that ‘set the tone,’ to say the least.

Tuchel is well aware of the challenge awaiting his players on Sunday, and England, since the World Cup and spirited Matchday 1 defeat, is performing with the precise swagger of a team that certainly believes it’s on an upward trajectory.
A thrilling contest is heading our way, with the visitor poised to embrace its newfound positional liberty up against the collective might of the world’s best.

FotMobSpain defeated Czechia without two key cogs in attack, as both Mikel Oyarzabal and Lamine Yamal were absent. However, the pair of forwards are expected to be back in action as La Roja host the Three Lions on Sunday.

Oyarzabal is one of several Spanish players who’s been dealing with an illness during this break, with Nico Williams and Aymeric Laporte also suffering. The latter two are doubtful for England’s visit, meaning Álex Baena should retain his spot down the left and Dean Huijsen will continue alongside Pau Cubarsí.
Atlético Madrid’s Marc Pubill scored off the bench on Thursday, and is in contention to replace Pedro Porro at right back.

World Cup Player of the Tournament Rodri is absent due to a hamstring injury, but De la Fuente is hardly shy of standout replacements. He opted for a Martín Zubimendi-Fabián Ruiz partnership last time out, with Pedri and Mikel Merino appearing off the bench. Pablo Barrios and Marc Roca are also on Spain’s November roster.
Spain predicted lineup vs. England (4-2-3-1): Simón; Porro, Cubarsí, Huijsen, Cucurella; Pedri, Fabián; Yamal, López, Baena; Oyarzabal.
FotMobTuchel is seemingly opting for continuity heading toward Euro 2028, with the German opting for the same front six against Croatia that started the World Cup semifinal against Argentina.

Morgan Rogers is currently deputizing for Bukayo Saka down the right flank, and Declan Rice has returned to the fold after missing the extended September-October break. Another midfield option, Alex Scott, is sidelined due to injury.

Tuchel has Myles Lewis-Skelly available after he served a one-match suspension, and there are hopes that his Arsenal teammate, Ezri Konsa, will be fit to feature against the world champion. England is unlikely to survive against this level of competition with a Jarell Quansah-Dan Burn center back partnership.
Djed Spence is also pushing to be available, with Trent Alexander-Arnold, omitted from the World Cup roster, getting the nod on Thursday.
England predicted lineup vs. Spain (4-2-3-1): Pickford; Alexander-Arnold, Konsa, Burn, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.
